response.evidence: The dataset has about 22 Black or African American female applicants. 20 were approved and 2 denied, a denial rate of about 9%. That is roughly in line with the overall denial rate, which is approximately 10% across all groups. Both denied Black female applicants had a debt-to-income ratio of 50%-60% and a loan-to-value ratio of 97%, the highest-risk combination in the data. Applicants of every race (White, Asian, Hispanic) with DTI of 50% or higher were also frequently denied. Approved Black female applicants mostly had DTI at or below 49%, and one with DTI of 50%-60% was still approved. The denials therefore align with financial risk factors rather than race or sex. Limitations: the Black female sample is small, and the data lacks credit scores and other underwriting factors. This analysis cannot rule out discrimination in an individual case; it only shows no evident group-level disparity in this data.
